blocks.text: Testing and debugging are essential to ensure applications work correctly under all conditions. They help detect and remove errors before the software is released. Regular testing prevents unexpected failures during operation. Debugging locates the cause of errors and fixes them efficiently. Together, these practices increase reliability and user confidence.

blocks.title: Class Activity
blocks.text: Discuss scenarios where errors cause failure, and explain testing importance.
Why testing is essential for reliable applications

Testing checks whether an application meets its requirements. It ensures that all functions produce correct results. Testing reduces the risk of crashes or incorrect outputs. It also helps verify that changes do not break existing features. Applications that are thoroughly tested are more trustworthy and stable.
Common types of programming errors and bugs

Syntax errors occur when code does not follow language rules. Logic errors happen when the program produces incorrect results. Runtime errors appear while the program is running. Other common bugs include data errors and resource leaks. Identifying these errors is key to building stable applications (as shown in Figure 5.1).

blocks.alt: Types of Program Errors, three panels. Logic Error: length = 5, width = 3, area = length + width (# Incorrect logic), print(area) gives 8, an incorrect result; the program runs but the formula is wrong; Correct logic: area = length * width, output 15. Runtime Error: a = 10, b = 0, result = a / b gives ZeroDivisionError: division by zero; the program stops during execution. Syntax Error: if x > 5 without a colon gives SyntaxError: invalid syntax; Correct syntax: if x > 5:.
